what: Lots of files with long filenames
title: Data analysis with idtools
text: common scenario faced genetic test development multiple files results, identifiers sample included long filenames. example 5 .csv files contain gene dosage results fictional patients. files saved folder called “data”. .csv file contains dosage (log2 ratio) results 5 genes interest. Table 1: Contents single .csv file order analyse data, two steps need completed: results individual file collated together one dataframe sample identifiers filename added dataframe separate columns. Collating file contents can achieved applying read_csv function readr files, using map function purrr. Specifying id="filepath" call read_csv adds full filepath new column contents file. creates dataframe containing results csv files. Table 2: Collated gene dosage data filepaths mutate_ids function idtools can applied new “filepath” column collated data. function extracts DNA lab number (labno), replicate suffix worksheet number filepath, adds identifier new column. Table 3: Collated gene dosage data separated identifiers Now data together single dataframe, including sample identifiers, can easily analysed. example, data can quickly filtered return results EGFR gene. Table 4: Results EGFR gene data can also filtered show results 3 different replicates sample 12345678. Table 5: Results sample 12345678 ggplot2 package tidyverse can used visualise results.  data folder also contains 5 Excel files quality control information. However, filename format different: identifiers different order csv files, hyphens used instead underscores. file contains “noise” metric sample replicate. Table 6: Contents single .xlsx file Similarly , contents xlsx files can collated together using readxl package. read_excel function readxl include option add filepath separate column, alternative approach use set_names “names_to” argument list_rbind achieve result. Table 7: Collated quality metric data filepaths , just csv files, identifiers can extracted using mutate_ids. Importantly, process still works even though filename format changed. Table 8: Collated quality metric data separate identifiers
code: csv_files <- list.files(path = "data/",            pattern = ".*.csv",            full.names = TRUE)  csv_files #> [1] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_12345678a_patient1.csv" #> [2] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_12345678b_patient1.csv" #> [3] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_12345678c_patient1.csv" #> [4] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_23456789_patient2.csv"  #> [5] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_34567890_patient3.csv" csv_data <- csv_files |>    purrr::map(\(csv_files) readr::read_csv(csv_files,                             id = "filepath",                             show_col_types = FALSE)) |>    purrr::list_rbind() csv_data_with_names <- csv_data |>    idtools::mutate_ids(id_col = filepath) knitr::kable(csv_data_with_names |>    dplyr::filter(gene == "EGFR")) knitr::kable(csv_data_with_names |>    dplyr::filter(labno == "12345678")) xlsx_files <- list.files(path = "data/",            pattern = ".*.xlsx",            full.names = TRUE)  xlsx_files #> [1] "data//Quality-control-patient1-12345678a-WS123456.xlsx" #> [2] "data//Quality-control-patient1-12345678b-WS123456.xlsx" #> [3] "data//Quality-control-patient1-12345678c-WS123456.xlsx" #> [4] "data//Quality-control-patient2-23456789-WS123456.xlsx"  #> [5] "data//Quality-control-patient3-34567890-WS123456.xlsx"  csv_files #> [1] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_12345678a_patient1.csv" #> [2] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_12345678b_patient1.csv" #> [3] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_12345678c_patient1.csv" #> [4] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_23456789_patient2.csv"  #> [5] "data//Gene_dosage_WS123456_34567890_patient3.csv" xlsx_data <- xlsx_files |>    purrr::map(\(xlsx_files) readxl::read_excel(xlsx_files)) |>    rlang::set_names(xlsx_files) |>    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "filepath") xlsx_data_with_names <- xlsx_data |>    idtools::mutate_ids(id_col = filepath)

what: Why is there no extract_patient_name function?
title: The scope of idtools
text: function extracting patient names idtools following reasons: Patient names always included filenames. Patient names may included filenames analysis performed using -prem servers, data analysed using cloud computing patient names removed. means datasets can include mixture files without patient names depending processed. samples people. samples control samples, mixtures different DNA samples cell lines. samples may given “name” may , name may may follow standard format “forename surname”. Example: “HorizonPositiveControl”. samples may research. Patient samples collected research anonymised, research identifier may included place sample name. research identifier may also include numbers non-letter characters. Example: “study0001” reasons mean designing regular expression identify patient name filename complicated. One option use position name string relative consistent identifiers, like lab number worksheet number, inflexible order identifiers changes. better approach get patient names databases iGene DNA Database.

what: Why is there no read_with_filename function?
title: The scope of idtools
text: Given idtools based around extracting identifiers filenames, earlier version included generic function read files dataframes add new column containing filename. prototype function shown , idea combined multiple read functions like readr::read_csv, readxl::read_excel vcfR::read.vcfR, piped mutate_ids. However, better options adding filepath new column reading files. readr::read_csv “id” argument, functions option using rlang::set_names purrr:list_rbind. options shown detail “Data analysis idtools” vignette.
code: read_with_filename <- function(filepath, read_fn) {    output <- read_fn(filepath, ...) |>     dplyr::mutate(filepath = filepath,                   filename = basename(filepath))    return(output)  }

title: Regular expressions for sample identifiers — regex_ids
text: worksheet: worksheet identifier "WS" followed six numbers, increase sequentially (.e "WS000001", "WS000002", WS000003"). Worksheets way genetic tests organised batches within lab. Worksheet identifiers generated DNA Database. labno: numeric identifier given every DNA sample DNA Database. regex specifies 8 digits identifier, although samples 2012 earlier 6 digits. identifier referred "labno" throughout idtools name used "Samples" table DNA Database. first two digits labno format year sample recieved, digits increase new sample. example, first sample recieved 2026 labno 26000001. suffix: DNA sample tested multiple times worksheet (can happen repeatability experiments test validation) suffix letter (usually -d) added directly labno. Extracting suffix useful assessing variability different replicates sample. igene_rno: R (referral) number iGene database format R followed two-digit year number, hyphen, four alpha-numeric charactes. Example: R26-AB12. igene_sno: S (sample) number iGene database format R number () S instead R beginning. combined_plate: combined plate number DNA Database "CP" followed 5 digits. wgs_patient_no: whole genome sequencing (WGS) pathway Genomic Medicine Service uses patient identifier "p" followed 11 digits. wgs_referral_no: referral ("r") equivalent WGS patient number, structured "r" followed 11 digits.
